name: Colour
lede: Colour is a brownish orange from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, named with the generic word for hue itself rather than any specific thing.

sections.title: The word for hue, as a hue
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* places this brownish orange on plate 12, cell L10, first recorded in 1898 [1]. Unlike most entries in the dictionary, the name is not a material, place or person; it borrows the general word "colour" itself, in its British spelling [1]. The same plate area carries related names Wild Honey (1926) and Rose Amber (1927), both warmer variants [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 report files the hue as a brownish orange [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[copper]], [[india-spice]], [[toffee]] and [[toffee]], at 3.7, 3.9, 4.2 and 4.2 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this orange-brown in 719 of 23,781 paintings, about 3 percent, as photographed [4]. The match peaks around 1420, with a lift nearly four times the archive's average rate for that decade, and the earliest dated hit is an Egyptian funerary papyrus, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. Painters including Filippino Lippi, Filippo Lippi, Gerard van Honthorst and Albrecht Dürer carry it often [4]. The count is a computed color match, not a pigment identification [4].
